editorial.description_en: A tile off an old roof, weathered on one face. Dark, red-brown, and much duller than the tile it started as.
editorial.description_ja: 古い屋根の瓦のような、暗い赤茶。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.344, C 0.058, h 46.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 古 (furu, old) + 瓦 (kawara, roof tile), rendaku to -gawara. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Old Tile" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 古瓦. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — doro-soko at ΔE00 5.5, do-ma at ΔE00 5.7, yaki-guri at ΔE00 5.8. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (226°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
